locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this scheduler acquires its locks? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: drainEncoder takes the encoder lock first and then each channel lock, while assign takes the channel lock first and then the encoder lock. If assign(ch1, encA) holds ch1's lock and is waiting for encA's lock while drainEncoder(encA) holds encA's lock and is waiting for ch1's lock, neither can make progress. The Mutex has no timeout, so both calls hang forever, and every later operation on that channel or encoder (including updateRenditions) queues behind them. drainEncoder should acquire locks in the same channel-then-encoder order (for example snapshot the channel ids, then lock each channel and then the encoder), or use one global ordering rule.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Two concurrent calls to updateRenditions for different channels arrive while assign(chX, encA) is awaiting store.persistAssignment. What happens?
choices: Both updateRenditions calls wait until the assign call finishes, because the mutex map is shared
Both proceed immediately unless one of them targets chX, which waits for assign to release chX's lock
All three operations are serialized because JavaScript is single-threaded
The updateRenditions calls fail with an error because chX's lock is held
choiceQuestions.explanation: Locks are per channel id (channelLock(id)). Only a call for chX contends with assign, which holds chX's mutex across the awaited persistAssignment. Other channels have their own Mutex instances, so they proceed. Single-threaded execution does not serialize async work across awaits, and Mutex.acquire waits rather than throwing.

choiceQuestions.prompt: When the holder of a Mutex calls its release function and there are waiters, what does Mutex.release do?
choices: Sets locked to false and lets all waiters race to set it again
Resolves every waiting promise so they run concurrently
Leaves locked as true and resolves only the oldest waiter, handing ownership directly to it
Throws if the release function is called by a different async context
choiceQuestions.explanation: release() shifts one waiter and calls its resolver without clearing locked, so ownership passes directly to the next waiter in FIFO order. locked only becomes false when no one is waiting. Nothing resolves all waiters, and the mutex does not track which context holds it.

choiceQuestions.prompt: assign throws 'encoder encA is full'. What is the state of the locks and data afterwards?
choices: Both locks are released by runExclusive's finally blocks and no assignment was persisted or applied
The encoder lock is released but the channel lock stays held, because the error escapes the outer callback
Both locks stay held until the process restarts
The assignment was persisted to the store but not applied in memory
choiceQuestions.explanation: The capacity check happens before persistAssignment, so nothing is written. The error propagates out of the inner runExclusive (whose finally releases the encoder lock) and then out of the outer one (whose finally releases the channel lock). No lock leaks, and the store is untouched.
